hook: Turing supplied both of AI's founding documents: the 1936 paper proving one universal machine could compute anything computable, and the 1950 paper asking whether machines can think. The first made computers possible; the second made artificial intelligence a research question rather than a fantasy.

reading.body:
Alan Turing's two most consequential contributions are distinct and should not be collapsed: the 1936 paper made universal computation mathematically possible, and the 1950 paper made machine intelligence a scientific question worth pursuing.

The 1936 work defined the abstract machine that every physical computer still instantiates. Without that theoretical foundation there is no architecture to build, no chip to fabricate, no data center to power. The 1950 paper then asked whether a machine running on that architecture could exhibit intelligence, and proposed an operational test rather than a philosophical one. That move transformed AI from speculation into a research program with a measurable target.

What the data does not cover is the path from these ideas to physical hardware, energy consumption, or scale. Turing worked in mathematics and logic, not in buildings or grids. The connection to compute infrastructure is real but indirect: his theoretical model is the ancestor of every processor that now drives AI workloads, but the data here stops at the intellectual origin and does not trace that descent. His life ended in 1954, two years after the state he had served prosecuted him, and decades before the scaling dynamics this site tracks came into view.

standing.watch: The records show nothing pending for Turing himself, no case, no planned listing, and no dispute. What remains unresolved is only what the site leaves unstated: the seven stories name him without recording any action, ownership, or outcome connected to him. The profile lists no open question beyond the historical ones already settled in its own text. Where the records are thin, they stay thin, and no future event involving Turing is identified. The watch section therefore rests on the absence of any pending matter in the supplied material.
standing.record: The site's records for Turing consist of a profile and seven news stories that name him. The profile supplies the two founding documents and the quick facts about the universal machine, Hut 8 at Bletchley Park, the imitation game, and the Turing Award. The seven stories are dated from August to October 2026 and concern ASML and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company revenue trends, NTT DATA's Addresstune expansion, Complete Financial Solutions projects in energy, manufacturing and sovereign AI compute, defense manufacturing and artificial intelligence, citizen-centric manufacturing for MSMEs, the Ulsan Forum on manufacturing AI, and India's manufacturing future. None of these stories describes a company founded by Turing, a case naming him, or a dispute involving him. The pattern is that his name appears in coverage of manufacturing and compute themes while the records themselves contain no current commercial or legal tie.
standing.standing: The records on this site place Alan Turing as the origin point rather than a current operator in artificial intelligence. He is credited with the 1936 paper defining the universal computing machine, the model every computer still follows, and the 1950 paper proposing the imitation game, now the Turing Test. The site also notes that the Turing Award, computing's highest honor, bears his name. Beyond those attributions, the records show no company he controls, no role he holds, and no influence he exercises today. His standing here is historical and foundational, not active.

timeline.event: Joins Bletchley Park the day after Britain declares war
Publishes Computing Machinery and Intelligence in Mind
Convicted of 'gross indecency' for his homosexuality
timeline.impact: Career destroyed by the state he had served

timeline.event: Receives royal pardon; 'Turing's Law' follows in 2017

quick_facts: Defined the universal computing machine (1936), the mathematical model every computer still follows
Led the Hut 8 team at Bletchley Park breaking German naval Enigma in WWII
Proposed the imitation game, now the Turing Test, in 1950
The Turing Award, computing's highest honor, bears his name

achievements.title: On Computable Numbers (1936)
achievements.impact: Introduced the Turing machine and universal computation, the theoretical basis of every computer built since.

achievements.title: Breaking naval Enigma at Bletchley Park (1939-1945)
achievements.impact: The bombe machines and Banburismus methods he devised shortened the Atlantic war; historians credit the effort with saving vast numbers of lives.

achievements.title: Computing Machinery and Intelligence (1950)
achievements.impact: Reframed 'can machines think?' as an operational test, predicted machine learning, and answered Lovelace's objection, the founding paper of AI.

achievements.title: The chemical basis of morphogenesis (1952)
achievements.impact: Founded mathematical biology with reaction-diffusion theory, showing his computational lens reached beyond machines.
